group: Counter machine with a doubling stage (Collatz-like coincidence)
title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0RA_1LA1RE_0LA0LB_0RB1RF_---1RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0RA_1LA1RE_0LA0LB_0RB1RF_---1RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced exactly to a three-counter map. Every time the head turns left into D the tape is X(a,b,c) = 1^a 0 (10)^b 1 D> 0 1^c, the same with 00 (Y), or Z(a,c) = 1^a 0 D> 0 1^c. Lean proves the 20 rules that take each shape to the next, for all values, and (kernel only, halts_iff in lean/Model.lean) that the machine halts from blank tape exactly when the orbit of X(2,0,3) reaches some Z(a,2). That needs a run of the Y rule whose middle block empties exactly when the right block holds 3 ones: impossible by parity in the doubling stage of a round, a chance of about 1/N elsewhere. 2,000 rounds of the map (N about 10756, about 101511 steps) show no halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,203 cells have been visited and 28,636 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.467). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.091).

claims.title: The 20 counter rules, for all values
claims.text: From each shape the machine reaches the next shape (or, from Z(a,2), the halting transition F0): for example X(a+4,b,c+2) → X(a+1,b+2,c+1) in 4b+13 steps and Y(a,b+1,c+2) → Y(a+3,b,c+1) in 4b+13 steps. Symbolic runs with the crossing lemmas.
claims.where: lean/Rules.lean (generated by py/gen_rules.py); in the shape of the map: r_*, rule_some, rule_none in lean/Model.lean

claims.title: From blank tape to X(2,0,3)
claims.text: After 29 steps from blank tape the tape is 1 1 0 1 D> 0 1 1 1 = X(2,0,3).

claims.title: Halting is the map reaching Z(a,2)
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of X(2,0,3) under nxt reaches a state where nxt is undefined, which is exactly Z(a,2).

claims.title: The map is the direct run up to 1.1·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A C simulation reads the tape at every left turn into D; every one of the 224,522 transitions up to 1.1·10<sup>10</sup> steps is the map's, with the map's step count.

claims.title: 2,000 rounds of the map
claims.text: Iterating the map with whole bulk runs at once (Python big integers): no halt in 2,000 rounds, about 10<sup>1511</sup> machine steps; N (the length of the all-ones tape at a round start) is about 10<sup>756</sup>.

claims.title: Almost surely nonhalting
claims.text: Halting needs c − b = 3 exactly at the start of a Y run. In the doubling stage b and c are both even, so it cannot happen there; in the rest of a round, if c − b behaves like a random number of size N, the chance is about 1/N per run, and the sum over all later rounds is negligible. The closest approach after round 3 was |c−b−3| ≈ 10<sup>−5.5</sup> N, over 2.5 million Y runs.

claims.title: Does the orbit ever reach Z(a,2)?
claims.text: The endgame of a round (after the doubling stage) has no closed form yet; without one there is no handle on the coincidence.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Lean: halting from blank tape is exactly the counter map reaching Z(a,2).
Of the map without halting, about 10<sup>1511</sup> steps.

sections.heading: Three counters on one tape
html:
Every time the head turns left into state D, the tape is one of

X(a,b,c) = 0^∞ 1^a 0  (10)^b 1 D> 0 1^c 0^∞
Y(a,b,c) = 0^∞ 1^a 00 (10)^b 1 D> 0 1^c 0^∞
Z(a,c)   = 0^∞ 1^a 0 D> 0 1^c 0^∞

a block of ones on the left, a block of 10s in the middle and a block of ones on the right, with the head between the last two. Between two such moments the head makes one trip over the middle block.

In X, each trip takes 3 ones from the left block, adds 2 10s to the middle block and uses one cell of the right block. In Y it is the other way round: the left block gains 3 and the middle block loses one 10. When a block runs out, a boundary rule switches between the shapes.

sections.heading: The counter map
html:
X(a+4,b,c+2) → X(a+1,b+2,c+1)    X(3,b,c+2) → X(1,b+1,c+1)    X(2,b,c+2) → X(2,b+2,c+1)
X(1,b,c+2)   → Y(3,b,c+1)        X(0,0,c+2) → Z(3,c+1)
X(a+5,b,1)   → X(a,0,2b+9)       X(4,b,1) → X(4,0,2b+7)       X(3,b,1) → X(4,0,2b+5)
X(2,b,1)     → X(0,0,2b+9)       X(1,b,1) → X(1,0,2b+5)
Y(a,b+1,c+2) → Y(a+3,b,c+1)      Y(a,0,c+2) → Z(a+3,c+1)      Y(a,b,1) → X(a,1,2b+3)
Z(a,c+6)     → X(a+4,0,c+1)      Z(a,1) → X(a,1,1)            Z(a,3) → X(a,0,5)
Z(a,4)       → X(a+2,0,3)        Z(a,5) → X(a+2,0,5)          Z(a,2): halts

Lean proves every rule for all values (lean/Rules.lean), that the run from blank tape is at X(2,0,3) after 29 steps, and that the machine halts exactly when the orbit reaches some Z(a,2) (halts_iff). The direct run agrees with the map, step counts included, for the first 1.1·1010 steps.

sections.heading: A doubling stage and an endgame
html:
A round starts at X(0,0,N): the whole tape is N ones. It opens with a doubling stage, five rules per lap:

X(A,0,C) → X(1,…) → Y(3,…) → Y(…,0,…) → Z(…) → X(2A+8, 0, C−A−6)

from A = 7 and C = N − 6, so A + 8 = 15·2i, until the right block is too short for another lap. A short endgame follows (sometimes with a second doubling stage) and ends at X(2,b,1) → X(0,0,2b+9), the next round.

sections.heading: One coincidence, never met
html:
The only way to halt is a Y run that starts with c − b = 3: its middle block empties when the right block has 3 ones, the next rule gives Z(a,2), and the machine reaches F reading 0. In the doubling stage b and c are both even, so this cannot happen there. In the endgame nothing rules it out, but c − b is a number of the size of N, so the chance is about 1/N.

Iterating the map for 2,000 rounds (N about 10756, about 101511 steps) shows no halt; the closest approach after round 3 was |c−b−3| ≈ 10−5.5 N. A proof would need a closed form of the endgame, which is not known.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.467). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.091).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,203 cells (28,806 left of the start, 67 right), with a density of 1s of 0.813.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Three-counter machine: proved in Lean to halt if and only if the orbit of X(2,0,3) under a 20-rule counter map reaches Z(a,2); the map has been followed for 2,000 rounds (about 10^1511 steps) without halting.
